47.0.0.en: 1 And after him rose up Nathan, and prophesied in the days of David. 2 As the fat is taken away from the sacrifice of salvation, so was David separated from among the children of Israel. 3 He played with lions as with kids, and with bears as if they had been lambs of the flock. 4 Did he not slay a giant when he was yet a youth? Did he not take away the reproach from his people, 5 when he lifted up his hand with the stone in the sling, and beat down the boasting of Goliath? 6 For he called upon the Lord the Most High; and He gave strength to his right hand, to slay a mighty warrior, and to exalt the horn of his people. 7 So the Lord gave him the glory of one who slays ten thousands, and praised him in His blessings, in that He brought to him the crown of glory. 8 For he destroyed the enemies on every side, and brought to naught the Philistines his adversaries, and brake their horn in sunder unto this day. 9 In all his works he gave thanks to the Holy One Most High with words of glory. 10 With his whole heart he sang praise, and loved Him that made him. 11 He set singers before the altar, and taught them sweet melodies. 12 He gave beauty to the feasts, and set in order the seasons unto the end, that they might praise His holy name, and that the sanctuary might sound from morning. 13 The Lord took away his sins, and exalted his horn for ever; He gave him a covenant of kings, and a throne of glory in Israel.

47.1.0.en: Sirach highlighted the following points: 1. David as a boy was a strong and courageous warrior in protecting the flock from lions and bears [3], and he also crushed Goliath the giant [4], and fought as a king against the Canaanites, especially the Philistines [5-7]. His main weapons in his battles were love for God and for his people and his prayers [5]; he did not forget to offer sacrifices of thanksgiving and praise to God, the Giver of victory [8-9]. 2. David's concern for communal worship [9] and for spreading the spirit of joy in the celebrations of the feasts [10]. 3. A man of sincere repentance, so he was made worthy to receive an everlasting royal covenant [11].

47.1.1.en: And after him rose up Nathan, to prophesy in the days of David [1].

47.1.2.en: He did not mention the fall of David, because his repentance wiped his sin from the record of his life. But lest we be lax about sin, he mentioned Nathan, who prophesied in his time, and who reproved the king for his sin and affirmed his need for firm discipline so that he might realize the bitterness of sin and not repeat it. The prophet Nathan rebuked King David for his fall into adultery with Bathsheba and for killing her husband in the battle (2 Kgs 12:1-15).

47.1.3.en: As the fat is taken away from the peace offering, so was David separated from among the children of Israel [2].

47.1.4.en: We should not be surprised at the comparison of David, the prophet and king, to the fat that is taken away from the peace offering. (See the appendix to this chapter.)

47.1.5.en: He played with lions as with young goats, and with bears as if they were lambs of the flock [3].

47.1.6.en: When Saul looked down on the youth David, and said to him: "Thou art not able to go against this Philistine to fight with him: for thou art but a youth, and he a man of war from his youth" (1 Sam 17:33). David answered him: "Thy servant kept his father's sheep, and there came a lion, and a bear, and took a lamb out of the flock: and I went out after him, and smote him, and delivered it out of his mouth: and when he arose against me, I caught him by his beard, and smote him, and slew him."

47.2.0.en: Did he not slay the giant in his youth, and take away the reproach from his people, when he lifted up his hand with the stone in the sling, and struck down the arrogance of Goliath? [4]

47.2.1.en: David went down with his staff and his sling and the smooth stones to strike the forehead of Goliath with a stone (1 Sam 17) and to kill him with his sword. His staff was a symbol of the Cross, and the stone is the Lord Christ (Ps 118:22), who kills the enemy.

47.2.2.en: St. Ambrose sees that the secret of David's victory is that he did not provoke the war, but Goliath was the one who began it, while David was driven into it by his spiritual zeal... He did not carry the weapons of Saul but his own sling and his staff... He entered the war after consulting the Lord. He says: [David did not provoke a war unless he was driven into it... His strength depended on his own arms and not on the weapons of others... He never entered a war without seeking the counsel of God [1].]

47.2.3.en: Would that in our spiritual striving we hold to these three things: that we do not push ourselves into the war by ourselves, but in humility flee from every stumbling block; then if we enter into a war, we carry our personal experience with our Lord and depend on His grace working in us, not on the prayers of others without striving on our part; and finally, that we do not go out to the war without seeking the counsel of the Lord and His help.

47.3.0.en: For he called upon the Lord the Most High, and strength was given to his right hand to overcome the mighty man in battle, and to exalt the horn of his people [5].

47.3.1.en: David took the instruments of Goliath to his tent, so that the energies that had been working for the kingdom of the devil might work for the Kingdom of God.

47.4.0.en: So they gave him the glory of one who slays ten thousands, and praised him with the blessings of the Lord, offering him the crown of glory [6].

47.4.1.en: The women received Saul and David, some of them singing to them and others beating the timbrels and triangles and repeating the refrain: "Saul hath slain his thousands, and David his ten thousands" (1 Kgs 18:2). Instead of rejoicing in David's success, Saul began to hate David, watching him. Envy filled the heart of Saul, and he wanted to be rid of David, who had saved him from his enemies. He wanted to kill David, and so became a bad example of anger and envy.

47.5.0.en: For he destroyed the enemies on every side, and brought to naught the Philistines who withstood him, and brake their power in sunder unto this day [7].

47.6.0.en: In every work of his he gave thanks to the Holy One Most High with a word of praise. And with his whole heart he sang a song of praise, and loved Him that made him [8].

47.6.1.en: David, the man of God, offered sacrifices of thanksgiving and praise as was his custom with all his heart, so his heart was counted like the heart of God (1 Kgs 13:13).

47.7.0.en: He set the singers of psalms before the altar, to send forth sweet melodies with their voices [9].

47.7.1.en: David made great preparations before his death. He did not prepare anything for the day of his death, but for the building of the house of the Lord. He devoted his life to a series of battles, not for the extension of the kingdom, but to gather materials for building the house of the Lord. In appearance he was one of the greatest heroes of war, while inwardly his heart was occupied with the building. St. Jacob of Serugh presents to us a wonderful picture of the feelings of King David as he was preparing to depart from the world, saying:

47.7.2.en: [When the one skilled in knowledge knew that his appointed time had come, he wished to show his love for the Lord plainly.

47.7.3.en: He saw death coming to dissolve the temple of his body, so he wished to build a holy temple for the Lord his God.

47.7.4.en: The prophet saw that the fabric of his body was almost worn out, so he wished to build the Holy of Holies for Him who holds the ends of the earth.

47.7.5.en: And when he showed the idea of building a temple, his Lord spoke to him by the Spirit, saying:

47.7.6.en: "O son of Jesse, build not for Me a temple of stones, for the heart of the righteous alone can contain Me, that I may be honored in it (2 Sam 7:5; Isa 66:1; Acts 7:46-50).

47.7.7.en: Heaven and earth with their bounds cannot contain Me, for only the heart of the righteous, and no other, can hold Me.

47.7.8.en: I am honored and sanctified in the pure soul, and a building made by the hands of men cannot contain Me.

47.7.9.en: Heaven, which is My throne, cannot hold Me in its bosom, and the earth alone is My footstool (Ps 99:5).

47.7.10.en: I have measured the heaven of the Most High with a span as One who knows all, and I have measured the dust of the earth in My hand as the Almighty (Isa 40:12).

47.7.11.en: Build not for Me a temple for My glory where I am to be honored, for your fingers have shed much of the blood of men.

47.7.12.en: Your son shall build Me a house to dwell in and to be sanctified in, and if it be well pleasing to Me, I shall be with him as I was also with you [2].]

47.8.0.en: He gave the feasts their honor, and arranged their times throughout the year, that they might praise the holy name of God, and that the sanctuary (the Temple) might resound from the early morning [10].

47.8.1.en: King David contributed the huge preparation for building the Temple in the days of his son Solomon, and encouraged the leaders and the people to contribute to the cost of the building. His wonderful efforts in organizing the choirs of praise and arranging the service of the feasts and of worship reveal what was in the heart of David. It did not concern him that the Temple be erected in his reign or that of his son, nor to estimate the cost of the building of the Temple, but he wanted to see the Temple as an icon of heaven rejoicing in the Lord, looking for every member of the people to contribute to the building of the Temple by enjoying the pledge of heaven.

47.8.2.en: Wherever David was, even in his flight from the face of Saul, who was determined to kill him, his harp and his praises did not leave him, so that heaven was not far from him, enjoying the divine presence under all circumstances.

47.8.3.en: The Lord forgave his sins, and exalted his standing [3] for ever, and gave him a covenant of kings and a throne of glory in Israel [11].

47.8.4.en: The covenant that the Lord made with David (2 Kgs 7:16) is that He would establish his throne for ever. This was fulfilled by the Incarnation of the Word of God from St. Mary, of the seed of David, and He is the King of kings. He establishes His Kingdom in the hearts of His believers from all the nations and peoples.

47.9.0.en: 14 After him rose up a wise son, and for his sake he dwelt at large. 15 Solomon reigned in days of peace, and God brought him rest on every side, that he might build a house for His name, and prepare a sanctuary for ever. 16 How wise wast thou in thy youth, and filled with understanding as a flood! For thy mind covered the earth, 17 and thou filledst it with dark parables. Thy name went far unto the islands; and for thy peace thou wast beloved. 18 The countries marvelled at thee for thy songs, and proverbs, and parables, and interpretations, 19 in the name of the Lord God, who is called the God of Israel. 20 Thou didst gather gold as tin, and didst multiply silver as lead.

47.9.1.en: David fell asleep while preparing the whole kingdom to fulfill the desire of his heart to build a house for the Lord, and he had devoted his resources for this work, and here he hands over the throne to Solomon, for no purpose except to fulfill the divine promise to him that his son would build the Temple. He fell asleep with a rejoicing heart, for he is a man of praise, feeling as one sharing the rejoicing life of the heavenly beings, and here his son Solomon builds the Temple, the house of praise and worship.

47.9.2.en: The Second Book of Chronicles begins with Solomon, whose main work was building the Temple as a center for the whole earth, declaring the divine presence. The book concentrated on the house of David so that believers might seek the Son of David dwelling in their midst and in their hearts. David fell asleep while preparing the whole kingdom to fulfill the desire of his heart to build a house for the Lord, and he had devoted his resources for this work, and here he hands over the throne to Solomon, for no purpose except to fulfill the divine promise to him that his son would build the Temple. He fell asleep with a rejoicing heart, for he is a man of praise, feeling as one sharing the rejoicing life of the heavenly beings, and here his son Solomon builds the Temple, the house of praise and worship.

47.9.3.en: After him rose up his wise son, who lived in a spacious place for his sake [12].

47.9.4.en: The period from the accession of Solomon to the throne in 961 BC until the captivity of Jerusalem by the Babylonians in 587 BC is long; he did not mention all the heroes of faith in that period, besides the fact that many of the kings in this period despised divine wisdom.

47.9.5.en: Solomon reigned in days of peace, and God gave him rest on every side, that he might build a house for His name, and prepare an everlasting temple [13].

47.9.6.en: Ben Sira was concerned to highlight what Solomon did to embrace heavenly wisdom, namely the building of the house of the Lord, where worship is practiced for the sanctification of the people [13], and his concern for songs, proverbs, wise sayings and interpretations [17].

47.9.7.en: Solomon built the Temple of the Lord in Jerusalem, and it was rebuilt by King Herod, and this building was contemporary with the coming of the Lord Christ, who prophesied its complete destruction (Mt 23:38-39), and that He would raise up a new temple, which is His body risen from the dead.

47.9.8.en: How wise you were in your youth! And full of understanding like a river! [14]

47.9.9.en: The Lord appeared to Solomon and asked him what he desired, and Solomon chose wisdom and did not ask for glory or riches (1 Kgs 3). God gave him what he asked and what he did not ask. He prayed, saying: "And thy servant is in the midst of thy people which thou hast chosen, a great people, that cannot be numbered nor counted for multitude. Give therefore thy servant an understanding heart to judge thy people, that I may discern between good and bad: for who is able to judge this thy so great a people?" (1 Kgs 3:8-9). It is said in the Book of Wisdom: "Wisdom is better than strength: and a wise man than a mighty man" (Wis 6:1). "Wisdom is glorious, and never fadeth away: yea, she is easily seen of them that love her, and found of such as seek her" (Wis 6:13).

47.10.0.en: Your soul covered the earth, and you were filled with parables and riddles [15].

47.10.1.en: "And God gave Solomon wisdom and understanding exceeding much, and largeness of heart, even as the sand that is on the sea shore" (1 Kgs 4:29). The secret of Solomon's glory is in the wisdom which he received as a gift from God, more than in wealth. Solomon experienced it as a divine gift, for he says: "For the Lord giveth wisdom: out of his mouth cometh knowledge and understanding" (Prov 2:6). And it is said in the Book of Job: "Who hath put wisdom in the inward parts? or who hath given understanding to the heart?" (Job 38:36).

47.11.0.en: Your name reached the far islands, and you became beloved for your peace [16].

47.12.0.en: And at your songs and your proverbs and your wise sayings the nations marvelled at you because of your interpretations [17].

47.12.1.en: Solomon was concerned to spread the spirit of wisdom among the nations; Solomon is counted unique in his concern for preaching to the nations through songs, proverbs, wise sayings and interpretations, and in being an example even to pagan kings in his work as a king.

47.12.2.en: The queen of Sheba marvelled at the wisdom of Solomon (1 Kgs 10): the queen confessed that what she saw was greater than what she had heard about him.

47.12.3.en: The greatness of his wealth: the queen of Sheba offered him much gold, spices and precious stones, and the kings of the surrounding nations also offered him in abundance.

47.12.4.en: The greatness of his generosity: much came to him, and he also gave much.

47.12.5.en: The greatness of his appearance: shields of gold, cups of gold, a throne unique in greatness.

47.13.0.en: The greatness of his power: chariots and horses in abundance [26].

47.13.1.en: His commercial ability: trade exchange with Egypt [28-29].

47.14.1.en: If all things are put together, it may be said that he surpassed all the kings of the earth in riches and wisdom at that time; he was a shadow of Christ, who said: "Behold, a greater than Solomon is here" (Mt 12:42; Lk 11:31).

47.14.2.en: In the name of the Lord God, who is called the God of Israel, you gathered gold as tin, and multiplied silver as lead. [18].

47.15.0.en: 21 Thou didst bow thy loins unto women, and by thy body thou wast brought into subjection. 22 Thou didst stain thy honor, and pollute thy seed: so that thou broughtest wrath upon thy children, and wast grieved for thy folly. 23 So the kingdom was divided, and out of Ephraim ruled a rebellious kingdom. 24 But the Lord will never leave off His mercy, neither shall any of His works perish, neither will He abolish the posterity of His elect, and the seed of him that loveth Him He will not take away. 25 Wherefore He gave a remnant unto Jacob, and out of him a root unto David.

47.15.1.en: After Solomon received great wisdom, fame and wealth from God, he went down and brought shame upon himself [20], and even enslaved himself to sexual passions. But God in His great mercy did not forsake him [22] for the sake of his father David, and indeed the Christ was born of the seed of David [22].

47.15.2.en: But you lay down beside women, and your body enslaved you [19].

47.15.3.en: His success is counted a testimony to God among the nations; yet with all the wisdom that marked him he fell into slavery to bodily lusts [19]. He turned away from true and pure worship through the seduction of his wives, a matter to which Holy Scripture pointed after several centuries (Neh 13:26); therefore God allowed him to be disciplined [9:11-40]. Solomon, who had consecrated his heart to the love of God, turned it to foreign women. Solomon, who began by shepherding his people with love, was occupied with his private palace and huge constructions, and so burdened his people with taxes and forced labor.

47.15.4.en: If Ben Sira himself followed in the footsteps of the wisdom of Solomon, then by the inspiration of the Holy Spirit he recorded this book in the pattern of the Book of Proverbs, though he affirms that the wise Solomon became corrupt because of his enslavement to idolatries and his withdrawal from the faith of his fathers.

47.15.5.en: v If you read again what was written about Solomon, you find that, although he was exceedingly wise (Eccl 12:9), he "drew near to many women," while the law of God says: "Neither shall he multiply wives to himself, that his heart turn not away" (see Deut 17:17). Despite the greatness of his wisdom and the greatness of his standing before God, he was deceived, because he gave himself over to many women. I think that the many women point to the many doctrines and the different philosophies that men have, which he, being a man rich in knowledge and wisdom, wanted to know and examine. He was not able to keep himself within the judgment of the divine Law.

47.15.6.en: He was seduced by the philosophy of Moab, which urged him to offer sacrifices to the idol of Moab. The same applies to the Ammonites and the other peoples.

47.15.7.en: It is said that he welcomed many women and built temples and offered sacrifices to their idols. Truly, it is a great thing to mingle with many doctrines as with women and yet not turn aside from the judgment of the truth, but to say firmly: "There are threescore queens, and fourscore concubines, and virgins without number. My dove, my undefiled is but one; she is the only one of her mother, she is the choice one of her that bare her" (Song 6:8-9) [4].

47.15.8.en: Origen: You brought a stain upon your glory, and defiled your seed, and brought wrath upon your sons, and they were pierced by your folly [20].

47.15.9.en: Therefore the kingdom was divided into two, and a rebellious kingdom arose out of Ephraim [21].

47.15.10.en: v Wisdom can be the greatest help in keeping company with the strongest men of the city, and it also usually knows when to exclude those who fail in doing their duty. For there has never been anyone who did not stumble. As for the words of the wicked, we must not give them final consideration, lest, hearing with your ears what is against you, you are then stung in the heart, and the reaction is your attacking him.

47.15.11.en: Although I knew all these things and had received wisdom from God, when I cast it from me I was no longer what I had been. For wisdom forsook me for a while to a distance that is hard to measure, so that it seemed it would never be mine. At last I stopped seeking it altogether, and I no longer cared to reckon my folly and my empty lusts and life of amusement [5].

47.16.0.en: St. Gregory the Wonderworker: But the Lord did not forsake His mercy, nor corrupt any of His words, nor blot out the seed of His elect (David), nor destroy the seed of him who loved Him, but He left a remnant for Jacob, and a root of his lineage for David [22].

47.16.1.en: For the sake of King David, the righteous, the Lord proclaimed His mercy, which was manifested in the following: 1. The repentance of Solomon and his return from corruption and his clinging to the Lord. 2. There were found among the kings of Judah (the southern kingdom) some godly ones who walked like their father David. 3. He left a holy remnant for Jacob, and the Lord allowed the discipline of Israel by the Assyrian captivity and the discipline of Judah by the Babylonian captivity, but He raised up Cyrus king of Persia to allow the Jews to return to the Promised Land. 4. The Lord raised up heroes of faith even in the land of captivity, such as Esther and Haman and the prophets Daniel and Ezekiel and others, and leaders such as Zerubbabel and Nehemiah and Ezra the scribe, etc. 5. The Lord did not break His covenant with David, so the Wisdom of God came incarnate from St. Mary, the daughter of David, and the incarnate King of kings established His Kingdom in the hearts of believers, and made of them a holy temple for Himself in which the Holy Spirit dwells.

47.17.s.en: 4. The rebellion of Jeroboam and the division of the kingdom

47.17.0.en: 26 And Solomon rested with his fathers, 27 and left behind him of his seed one foolish among the people, 28 even Rehoboam, of little understanding, who turned away the people through his counsel, 29 and Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin, and gave Ephraim a way of sin. And their sins were multiplied exceedingly, 30 until they were removed out of their land, 31 and sought out all wickedness, till the vengeance came upon them.

47.17.1.en: The degradation of Solomon through his slavery to lusts bore fruit in the division of the kingdom immediately after his death. Corruption passed to his sons, beginning with Rehoboam [23]. Because of his indulgence in lusts and his rebellion against the divine commandment, Solomon took foreign wives who worshiped idols. So he planted the seeds of rebellion and disobedience in his son Rehoboam. This is what he also planted in his former servant Jeroboam, who turned from a friend of Solomon and his seed into a rebellious enemy. The rebellion of both Rehoboam and Jeroboam led to the division of the kingdom into a northern kingdom comprising ten tribes under the leadership of Jeroboam, and a southern kingdom comprising two tribes, Judah and Benjamin. This division drove the ten tribes to become estranged from Jerusalem and the Temple and the Levitical priesthood, and to be plunged into idolatry.

47.17.2.en: When Solomon rested with his fathers, he left after him one of his sons, lacking prudence and understanding.

47.17.3.en: Rehoboam, who by his counsel led the people to rebel [6] [23].

47.17.4.en: Two kings succeeded Solomon, one in the south, his son Rehoboam, and the second in the north, his enemy Jeroboam, and both of them were foolish [23].

47.17.5.en: Likewise there was Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who drove Israel to sin, and led Ephraim in the way of sin, and their sins were multiplied exceedingly until He removed them from their land [24].

47.17.6.en: They sought after all evil, until the punishment came upon them [25].

47.17.7.en: v Question: How can we fear the judgment of God (Heb 27:10)?

47.17.8.en: Answer: The expectation of anything terrifying drives a person to fear. So we fear wild beasts, and also rulers, expecting some evil from them. Therefore if a person believes that God's warnings about the final judgment are true, and expects that it is fearful and terrifying, it is natural for him to fear the judgments of God [7].

47.17.9.en: St. Basil the Great Inspired by Sirach 47

47.18.s.en: Fence me about with Your grace, lest I collapse

47.18.0.en: v Whenever I look at Rehoboam the son of Solomon the son of David, my depths cry out to You that my soul may not perish.

47.18.1.en: Rehoboam did not learn from his father Solomon, so as to ask wisdom of You.

47.18.2.en: He took the counsel of the wicked, and was arrogant toward the people.

47.18.3.en: So all that his wise father and his godly grandfather had gathered was lost.

47.18.4.en: v The young Solomon began to rule, and he asked for wisdom that he might hand over the leadership of the kingdom into Your hand; he increased in glory and wisdom and wealth, and the world was amazed at his wisdom.

47.18.5.en: But he became careless, and gave over his loins beside pagan women.

47.18.6.en: He brought a stain of shame upon his glory, and defilement upon his seed, and wrath upon his sons.

47.18.7.en: Yes, he repented, but his son Rehoboam had absorbed corruption from him in the period of his deviation!

47.18.8.en: v And what shall I say of David, the grandfather of Rehoboam? In his early youth he tore a lion and a bear with his hands.

47.18.9.en: He faced Goliath the giant, not with sword and spear, but in Your name, O Lord of hosts, and he crushed his arrogance against You.

47.18.10.en: His life was an unbroken series of praises and thanksgivings to You.

47.18.11.en: He established holy choirs that praise with the heavenly beings.

47.18.12.en: He organized the joyful feasts, and prepared many for the everlasting heavenly feast.

47.18.13.en: One day he grew lax, and descended from sin to sin. So You sent him the prophet Nathan to bring him back to You by repentance.

47.18.14.en: There is no one, even a great prophet or a king beloved by You and by men, who is immune from error!

47.18.15.en: Fence me about, O Lord, lest I grow lax like great David, nor give myself up to careless gatherings like wise Solomon, nor run after unfitting friendships like Rehoboam!

47.18.16.en: There is none to protect me from my weaknesses except Your Holy Spirit!

47.18.17.en: Appendix to Sirach 47: David the prophet and the fat in the peace offering. Ben Sira compares the prophet David among the children of Israel to the fat in the peace offering (Sir 47:2; Lev 3).

47.18.18.en: First: As for the peace offering, Origen [8] sees it as the offering of the perfect man, or the spiritually mature, who enjoys the perfect peace of God in his inner life, and as an overflow of peace and thanksgiving springing from the Lord Christ, the Giver of peace. Therefore it is called "the offering of perfection."

47.18.19.en: Second: As for the fat, in the Old Testament the eating of blood and fat was forbidden, because the blood points to the life of man, and the fat is the best part of the animal. The commandment came in the peace offering that the man who eats the fat of this sacrifice shall be cut off from the people of God (Lev 3:16). The fat was offered to the Lord and man had no share in it, a sign of offering the best thing in the sacrifice to the Lord. And when Eli the priest was lax with his two sons the priests, letting them eat the fat of the sacrifices, the Lord rebuked him, for he honored his sons above the Lord (1 Sam 2:29).

47.18.20.en: It is said of the peace offering: "And he shall offer of the sacrifice of the peace offering an offering made by fire unto the Lord; the fat thereof, and the whole rump, it shall he take off hard by the backbone; and the fat that covereth the inwards, and all the fat that is upon the inwards, and the two kidneys, and the fat that is upon them, and the priest shall burn them upon the altar: it is the food of the offering made by fire unto the Lord" (Lev 3:9-11).

47.18.21.en: Third: David and his being chosen from among Israel is likened to the fat in the best sacrifice, which belongs to the perfect. He is the portion of the Lord, for he consecrated all his life, and especially his heart and his thought and his emotions, to the Lord alone. So David was a living model of those who do what is right in the eyes of the Lord (1 Kgs 11:33; 2 Kgs 22:2; 2 Chr 28:1).

47.18.22.en: This is the personality which enjoyed the divine promise that from its seed one would sit on the throne for ever.

47.18.23.en: Ben Sira presents David as the best of the perfect ones, and yet with this loftiness he was not immune from error; and when he was lax in the purity of his heart he fell into sins into which he had not fallen in his boyhood and youth. Truly, he spent the rest of his life practicing repentance with a spirit of hope and certainty in the love of God who forgives sins!

47.18.24.en: [What is wonderful in the plan of God is that the drinking of blood and the eating of fat are harmful to man's health; and at the same time the Law forbade eating them because they are the portion of the Lord.]
